The Trump administration's actions to support equity markets at all costs comes at a drastic expense to the lower and middle income citizens and small and medium sized businesses, the exact people who elected him into office for change.

They are falling further and further behind.

These equity market focused stimulus measures are creating inflation and add fuel to the fire burning down the lower and middle class by forcing the Fed to hike interest rates. These front-end interest rate hikes have an outsized negative impact on small businesses while the administration's suppression of long-end yields benefit the wealthy and long-term corporate borrowers.

These are all measures the Trump administration and its top officials (@SecScottBessent et al) campaigned against and vowed to fix, but they continue the same policy path that has led to the most imbalanced and unequal economy and wealth divide in decades.

There's a reason this administration has record low approval ratings and rapidly deteriorating polling numbers going into midterms. They continue to worsen the economic hardship onto the workers least able to bear it and least able to articulate what is happening to them while making the rich richer and ensuring the top 1% and technology oligarchs continue to reap the rewards.

When you truly understand the ramifications of what's happening at the direction of policymakers and elected officials who were voted into office to do the opposite, and assuming you have a human heart and conscious, it's hard not to adopt a "burn it down" view.

I've been seeing comparisons between @worldnetwork and @Concordium on my TL for the past few days.

Most people get the idea wrong.

Both are building trust infrastructure for AI agents, but in very different ways.

World uses iris biometrics to prove someone is a unique human. Its AgentKit extends that human proof to agents.

Concordium is an AI project where identity sits in the protocol itself, so you can prove who's behind a wallet or an AI agent.

Its Agent Registry links agents to verified people or businesses, while ZK proofs let users prove attributes without exposing the underlying identity, and $CCD pays network fees.

Proving you’re over 18 without revealing your birth date is a good example.

As AI agents start holding wallets and moving money, proving who stands behind them becomes critical.

This is a bigger week than most investors realize for $SPCX and they’re just scratching the surface.

Monday: Starship’s first orbital mission deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites.

Thursday: Three launches. First, a Falcon 9 launch from Florida with four crew members going to the International Space Station. Second, Falcon 9 will launch from California with 103 payloads. Third, Falcon Heavy will launch NROL-97, a U.S. spy satellite, from Florida (a different pad than the one earlier in the day).

Long-Term Launch Targets: This year, SpaceX will do about 170-180 missions. In August, Musk said that by 2030, the goal is 30 Starship launches a day. If they run Mon-Fri, that’s 6k a year. In other words, we’re 3% of the way there.

The Key Question: What is the real launch number in 2030? I believe a more likely number is 2,200 by 2030, which implies about doubling every year. If they get to that 2k-plus number, my guess is the stock more than doubles from here. A double would imply an average annual return of 30% during those four years.
